To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Nuclear pharmacy instruction is not a required component of the PharmD curriculum in most pharmacy schools.

the majority of colleges and schools of pharmacies do not offer nuclear pharmacy instruction, that when it is taught it is usually in the first two years, and that the majority of instruction is focused on dispensing.

82% of pharmacy programs do not offer any instruction in nuclear pharmacy, 18% offer some instruction in nuclear pharmacy and 10% of the programs that offer nuclear pharmacy instruction include material relevant to clinical nuclear pharmacy practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of nuclear reactions, and how they can be exploited for practical applications.
the development of new methods for the preparation of radiopharmaceutically useful compounds and with the study of the pharmacology of these agents.
the development of a new generation of materials for the construction of nuclear power plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of colleges and schools of the United States and Canada offer no formal instruction in nuclear pharmacy in the PharmD program.
the current status of the teaching of nuclear pharmaceuticals in colleges and schools in the United States and Canada is inadequate and needs improvement.
nuclear pharmacy instruction in schools of pharmacy is limited and not consistent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the ability of a single, small molecule, which can be administered in an oral dosage form, to inhibit both the growth of tumors as well as the development of new blood vessels.
we have demonstrated a need for nuclear medicine training in pharmacy schools and we have developed a model for a nuclear medicine curriculum for pharmacy schools.
we are working with the nuclear pharmacy community to improve the quality of the nuclear pharmacist and nuclear pharmacy technician.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear pharmacy instruction is not a priority in many schools and that, in general, the focus of instruction is on dispensing rather than clinical practice.
there is no single best way of teaching nuclear medicine to students in pharmacy schools.
there are many ways to approach the teaching of nuclear medicine in pharmacy schools and that there is no right answer for all institutions.
